facts.text: Rathaus Schöneberg, completed in 1914, was the city hall of West Berlin until 1991 when the capital moved back to Mitte.
Since the 1920s, Nollendorfplatz has been the beating heart of Berlin’s gay community, a tradition that survived the Weimar era and beyond.
The famed Comedian Harmonists formed in 1927 in the Friedenau neighborhood of Schöneberg, launching a new era of German popular music.
From 1948 to 1993, RIAS Berlin’s radio studios in Schöneberg broadcast the first American‑controlled radio station in the city, later becoming DeutschlandRadio.
Schöneberg’s urban tapestry includes the affluent Bavarian Quarter and the historic Rote Insel, each reflecting distinct cultural layers of the locality.
The village of Schöneberg first appeared in a 1264 deed issued by Margrave Otto III of Brandenburg, marking its earliest recorded history.
